title: Love: A Biblical Perspective
description: Chapter 2 summary and homework from Marriage Enrichment 2022

gospel_data.title: Love: A Biblical Perspective

nestedSubsections.title: FEELINGS:
nestedSubsections.content:
It is very common for marriages to be built predominantly on a foundation of feelings. The feeling of being “in love” is powerful and it motivates many couples into getting married.

  1. Feelings are fickle.

    1. Amnon and Tamar 2 Samuel 13:10-14.
      2 Samuel 13:15 Then Amnon hated her with a very great hatred, for the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said, “Get up, go away!”

      1. Amnon’s supposed love for his sister was the feeling of being “in love,” however there was no lasting substance to it.

    2. Dr. Stuart Scott rightly states, “While there may be something that individuals fall in and out of, it is not true love.”1

    3. When controlled by feelings instead of good judgment, bad things happen:

      1. A Christian might sinfully marry a non-believer 2 Corinthians 6:14.

      2. A woman may marry a man with a severe drinking problem thinking he will quit for her Ephesians 5:18.

      3. A man might marry a woman who is very contentious, but he thinks she will change for him Proverbs 21:9.

      4. A person might even get involved with someone who is married, because they are “in love,” and so it must be right Exodus 20:14!

  2. The “feeling of love,” though wonderful, is not by itself substantial or solid enough a foundation to hold the weight of a marriage relationship.

nestedSubsections.title: PHYSICAL ATTRACTION:
nestedSubsections.content:
Sometimes the desire and passion that people have for each other based on physical appearance are mistaken for love.

  1. Dr. Stuart Scott states, “Appreciation, desire or passion that is initiated by and/or based upon outward appearance is not true love.”2
    Proverbs 31:30 Charm is deceitful and beauty is vain, But a woman who fears the LORD, she shall be praised.

  2. Our culture has stressed physical attractiveness to the point where it is now considered by some as a legitimate need for most men.

    1. Harley states, “that most men have a need for an attractive wife.”3

    2. This statement is not only unscriptural 1 Timothy 6:8, but it puts a tremendous amount of pressure on women to be attractive.

  3. Physical attraction is not a solid enough foundation to establish a marriage, nor does it constitute biblical love.

nestedSubsections.title: SEX:
nestedSubsections.content:
Sex is often equated with love. This is understandable since engaging in sexual relations usually involves passion and desire, both of which are strong feelings associated with love.

  1. Dr Stuart Scott rightly states that, “Many believe that love is synonymous with the sex act. Like physical attraction, the sex act can be nothing more than selfish lust.”4

    1. While sexual relations are supposed to be reserved for the expression of love in heterosexual marriages, however sinful sexual acts such as prostitution, incest, rape, and adultery do occur and prove beyond a doubt that the sexual act in and of itself does not constitute love.

      1. Wheat states, “The world for centuries has tried to convince people of the notion that secretive adulterous love is more exciting than love in marriage.”5
        Proverbs 5:3 For the lips of an adulteress drip honey And smoother than oil is her speech.

  2. Sexual acts within the bounds of a biblical marriage can and should express love, but it should not be equated with love. It is just as capable of expressing selfishness and lust.

nestedSubsections.title: NEEDINESS:
nestedSubsections.content:
Another unbiblical view of love is neediness. Neediness is self focused and is much more selfish than it is loving.

  1. An attitude of neediness is being propagated in many eclectic Christian books. For instance, the book Love & Respect teaches that “She needs unconditional love and he needs unconditional respect.”6

    1. The perceived need for love and respect are in fact, desires, not needs.

nestedSubsections.title: Unbiblical view of love summarized.
nestedSubsections.content:
1. There are many differing views of what constitutes love, but most of them are self-focused and motivated by what they will receive rather than what they can give.

  2. Many marriages have been founded on the basis of feelings, but when the feelings fade, they conclude that the relationship is over.

    1. When a couple’s marriage is established and held together primarily on the basis of feelings, divorce is a very real danger.

  3. Wrong views of love are generally “feeling” oriented and at the same time self-centered.

nestedSubsections.content:
Biblical love is an action, not a feeling.
Luke 10:27 You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself.

  1. Jay Adams rightly defines biblical love, stating, “Love is not feeling first. Before all else it is the determination to do good for another person because God has told you to do so. Love begins therefore, with a desire to please God. Love toward another is a willingness to give to him whatever you have that he needs, because you know God wants you to. Where true love exists, the feelings follow soon enough.”7

    1. Couples who love in a biblical manner choose to love each other as an act of the will. They are determined to love each other because they know it pleases God, Ephesians 5:25 , Titus 2:4.

  2. Dr Stuart Scott defines love as “a selfless and enduring commitment of the will to care about and benefit another person by righteous, truthful, and compassionate thoughts, words, and actions.”8

  3. Biblical love then must be understood as a commitment; it must be grasped as an action and not a feeling.

  4. A contrast between feeling-oriented love and biblical love is often displayed when marriages go through rough times.

    1. The feeling-oriented man might say to his wife during a particularly rough time, “I’ve never loved you.”

      1. Thomas states, “This is meant to be an attack on the wife saying in effect, ‘the truth is, I’ve never found you loveable.’ But put in a Christian context, it’s a confession of the man’s utter failure to be a Christian. If he hasn’t loved his wife, it is not his wife’s fault, but his. Jesus calls us to even love the unlovable-even our enemies!- so a man who says, ‘I’ve never loved you’ is a man who is saying essentially this: ‘I’ve never acted like a Christian.’ ”
        1 Corinthians 13:4-8 Love is patient, love is kind and is not jealous; love does not brag and is not arrogant, does not act unbecomingly; it does not seek its own, is not provoked, does not take into account a wrong suffered, does not rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never fails.

    2. When a couple has run into problems because they no longer “feel” in love, the solution is to confess their lack of love as sin, repent, and put on biblical love. They need to repent of their self focus and become other-focused.

    3. Jay Adams states that, “They do not vow to receive companionship, but to provide it for one another. Marriage itself is an act of love in which one person vows to meet another’s need for life, no strings attached.”9

    4. The solution for couples who no longer “feel in love” is to confess their lack of love as sin, repent, and put on biblical love. John 13:17.

    5. Smith wisely states, “The will is like a wise mother in a nursery; the feelings are like a set of clamoring, crying children. The mother makes up her mind to a certain course of action which she believes to be right and best. The children clamor against it and declare it shall not be. But the mother, knowing that she is mistress and not they, pursues her course lovingly and calmly in spite of all their clamors; and the result is that the children are sooner or later won over to the mother’s course of action, and fall in line with her decisions, and all is harmonious and happy. But if that mother should for a moment let in the thought that the children were the masters instead of herself, confusion would reign unchecked. And in how many souls at this very moment is there nothing but confusion, simply because the feelings are allowed to govern, instead of the will.”10

    6. Simply put, the Christian must not let his feelings be the foundation of his marriage, but rather he must be determined to love his spouse as an act of the will because he desires to be pleasing to God.

  1. Stuart Scott, The Exemplary Husband: A Biblical Perspective, 105.

  2. Stuart Scott, Exemplary Husband, 103.

  3. Willard Harley, His Needs, Her Needs: Building an Affair-Proof Marriage, 112.

  4. Scott, Exemplary Husband, 103.

  5. Ed Wheat, Love Life: How to Fall in Love, Stay in Love, Rekindle Your Love, 15.

  6. Emerson Eggerichs, Love and Respect: The Love She Most Desires, The Respect He Desperately Needs, 69.

  7. Jay E. Adams, What Do You Do When Your Marriage Goes Sour?, 1-2.

  8. Scott, Exemplary Husband, 106.

  9. Jay E. Adams, Solving Marriage Problems: Biblical Solutions for Christian Counselors, 22.

  10. Hannah Whitall Smith, The Christian’s Secret of a Happy Life.

subsections.title: Homework Questions
subsections.content: Complete the exercises below and save your answers.

questions.question: Memory Verse: Philippians 2:3-4 Do nothing from selfishness or empty conceit, but with humility of mind regard one another as more important than yourselves; do not merely look out for your own personal interests, but also for the interests of others.
Scripture: Read Luke 10:27 with your spouse and answer the question, “Is God commanding us to “feel” something or to “do” something?”
Review and discuss this lesson with your spouse.
Pray daily to love your spouse and to be a better companion.

Application

  • Make a list of at least 10 good things you can do for your spouse.

  • If you are having trouble making this list, enlist your spouse’s help.

  • Begin to do these things, at least three per week.

  • Do it because it is pleasing to God.

  • Keep a record of it, keep doing it.
